2. This Rule for Contempt of Court was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the proceeding for contempt of court should not be drawn up against them for not complying with the judgment and decree passed by the courts. 

 4. Challenging this order of termination dated 31•8-82 the petitioner filed a suit being Title Suit No. 697 of 1985 for a declaration that the order of termination dated 31-8-82 was illegal, void and without lawful authority and prayed for re-instatement to the service as Secretary of the BSC with all financial benefits. In that suit both the Ministry of Shipping and the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation were defendants. Ultimately, the petitioner obtained a decree on 22-6-89 in the aforesaid suit with a declaration that the termination of his service was illegal and without jurisdiction and he should be re-instead to his former service as Secretary of the BSC with all financial arrear benefits. Against the judgment of the trial Court the defendants preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 223 of 1989. After hearing the parties the Lower Appellate Court passed a judgment dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court by a judgment dated 17-2-91. Against the judgment of the Lower Appellate Court the defendants preferred a Civil Revision Case namely, CR No.1380 of 1991. In that matter, Rule was issued and after hearing both sides the High Court Division discharged the Rule and affirmed the judgment and decree of the Courts below by its judgment dated 7-4-93 with a cost of Taka 5,000.00 to be given to the petitioner by the opposite parties. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the High Court Division, the defendants preferred appeal before the Appellate Division and the appeal was registered as CPLA No. 286 of 1992. On 2-3-94 the Appellate Division granted leave only to hear in respect of back salaries, termination benefits, etc. But leave against re-installment was dismissed and accordingly, stay allowed earlier against 

 9. On the same day by letter dated 9-5-95 the Ministry of Shipping directed the BSC to take disciplinary action against the officer who earlier made correspondence with the Ministry unauthorisedly in the matter. On May 21, 1995 the new person Mr SM Shamsul Alam joined as Managing Director of the BSC which is annexed as Annexure-27 to the supplementary affidavit of the petitioner. After joining on 21-5-95 the new Managing Director issued a letter on 25-5-95 for re-instatement of the petitioner to his service. In that letter it was stated that in obedience to the order of the Hon'ble Courts for re-instatement in the service and in reference to the previous correspondence the petitioner was requested to report forthwith at the petitioner Head Officer. This letter is annexed: as Annexure-28 to the supplementary affidavit. In pursuance of the aforesaid letter dated 25-5-95 the petitioner joined and reported for his duties as Secretary on 4-6-95 on the basis of his joining letter dated 31-3-94 and the BSC notified the same accordingly. In this connection it may be mentioned that the Appellate Division by its judgment dated 13-5-96 dismissed the Civil Appeal No. 18 of 1994 with Civil Appeal No. 30 of 1994 preferred by the BSC and the Government respectively with costs and allowed the petitioner to have all arrear financial benefits as per decree and this judgment of the Appellate Division is annexed as Annexure-I to the affidavit in reply of the petitioner. 

 11. In this Rule, contemner No: 1 SA Iqbal filed a counter affidavit denying the allegations madein the application for contempt of court. It is the case of the contemner No. 1 that the petitioner did neither go to the office of the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation at Chittagong to submit his so-called joining report as alleged nor did he actually appear before the concerned authority to join his duties in the office as Secretary. His letter dated 31-3-94 addressed and sent to the contemner No. 1 raised disputed questions of fixation of his seniority and also giving him higher position of General Manager as contition precedent. The question of seniority and promotion to the higher post of General Manager are matters which may come up for consideration and  decision by the Board upon presentation of all facts and consideration thereof only after his joining his duty as Secretary according to the decree of the trial Court. The decree of the trial Court was for re-instating him to the posi of Secretary which he was holding at the time of termination of his service under the corporation. The order No. 10 of 1982 by which the petitioner was transferred to the Secretaryat department of the corporation clearly stated that he will carry his post and rank to the new Department which means that he was made Secretary without being promoted to the rank of General Manager and, as such, promotion to the higher post and seniority are matters which are beyond the decision of the trial Court in TS No. 697 of 1985.  Thus the letter dated 31-3-94 written by the petitioner could not be considered to be a joining  report nor construed to be an expression of his  intention to act according to the decree passed by the  trial Court in TS No. 697 of 1985 as affirmed up to  the Appellate Division. 

 12. Further, it is stated that in the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court the petition for leave to appeal No. 39 of 1994 was pending. On receipt of the letter from the Ministry, the corporation asked the petitioner to join his service in the BSC but the  petitioner avoided to do so and rushed to file an  application for drawing up contempt proceeding against him and another officer of the corporation. It is further stated that he could simply join as Secretary as he was holding the post at the time of termination of his service. But since he never appeared in the corporation in person to join his duties as Secretary as per decree, there is no question of contempt or disregard or disobedience to the judgment of the Supreme Court and other courts as  alleged. He simply submitted his application for joining with conditions and, as such, his application for joining was not considered. This contemner No.  1 stated that he never showed disrespect or dis-obedience to the judgment of the court as alleged. 

 15. In this connection let us see the joining report of the petitioner dated 31-3-94 vide Annexure- E to the petition which was addressed to the Managing Director, Bangladesh Shipping Corporation, namely, the Contemner No.1 and this letter was given personally by the present petitioner. The subject of this letter shows prayer for allowing the petitioner to join as the Secretary of the BSC in compliance with the verdict given by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. In that letter he had given background of the whole case and in paragraph 6 he stated that he had already submitted his joining report on 25th July, 1989 with the BSC Secretary of the Corporation after he obtained the decree from the trial Court. In paragraph II he had stated as follows: "Since the order of termination of my service from BSC as Secretary with effect from 31-8-1982 has been consistently found by all the courts including the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court as illegal and malafide and the Appellate Division has withdrawn its earlier order staying against my re-instatment as the Secretary of BSC I do hereby submit by Joining report (afternoon) today as Secretary of the Corporation and would, therefore, fervently request you to accordingly accept my joining with immediate effect as per verdicts of all the courts of the country inclining the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. In this connection, it may be mentioned that since the termination of my service dated 31-8-82 has been declared illegal and malafide even by the highest court of the country ie, Appellate Division of the Supreme Court, I should be kindly treated to have been always in service from the above date of termination." 

 16. In other paragraph of the above letter dated 31-3-94 though he had given some background of his case and also in paragraph 12 lie has made prayer seeking some other relief, but, in fact, the paragraphs show that he appeared in the office of the BSC at Chittagong and submitted his joining report personally, From paragraph 6 it further shows that after obtaining decree in the trial Court he also submitted this joining report on 25th July, 1989. The petitioner also filed another application for joining his service as Secretary on 23-4-94 and it was addressed to Me SAM Iqbal, Managing Director and Mr AKM Golam Faruque, General Manager (Admn) and Acting Secretary, In this letter also in concluding paragraph No. 12 the petitioner stated as follows: "I would, therefore, once again most fervently urge upon the management to accept my joining report and allow me to join the Corporation as Secretary by cancelling BSC's earlier order of termination of my service dated 31-8-82 in compliance with court's order without any further delay." 

 17. In this case opposite party No.2 is Me AKM Golam Faruque. At the relevant time, after the termination of the service of the petitioner, this contemner No.2 was acting as Acting Secretary of the BSC. In the affidavit he has stated that while he was serving as General Manager and Acting Secretary of the Corporation, he had to sign the letter addressed to the petitioner dated 2-4-94 in due course of his official duties. The Contemner No. 2 did not do any other act in connection with the petitioner's joining the service of the corporation as Secretary in purusance of the decree passed by the courts in his favour. He has further stated that he is a law abiding citizen having deepest regard and respect for the courts of the country and cannot conceive of violation of any order of the court nor has he, to the best of his know ledge, violated one at any time. The allegations of the petitioner against him are not all all correct 

 18. Me Mainul Hosein and Me Rokanuddin Mahmud, the learned Advocates are appearing for the petitioner while Me Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with his learned Junior Me SM Moonir has appeared on behalf of the contemner Nos. 1 and 2., The learned Advocates for the petitioner have submitted that even after the order of the Appellate Division and submission of the joining report by the petitioner in person going to the Head Office of BSc; at Chittagong, the contemner No. 1 who was the Managing Director of the Corporation, with deliberate intention flouted and showed dishonour and disrespect to the judgment of the court by not implementing the judgment and decree passed in favour of the petitioner. They have referred to the different annexures to the contempt petition as well as affidavit-in-reply and supplementary affidavit. It is their case that this contemner No.1 was the Managing Director since 1992 upto 16th of April, 1995. They submit that after the Judgment of the Appellate Division and even after issuance of the contempt rule Government in the Ministry of Shipping directed for five times to the Contemner No.1 to implement the courts Judgment by allowing the petitioner to join as Secretary of the BSC. The contemner No.1, the Managing Director of the Corporation, showed total disrespect even to the orders of the Ministry by showing this reason or that. 

 21. We have heard the learned Advocates of both sides and perused the application, counter affidavit, affidavit in reply and the supplementary affidavit and all the annexures adduced by the petitioner and the contemners. Mr Khandaker Mahabubuddin Ahmed submits that the petitioner simply sent a letter for joining to the post, but he never went to the office of the corporation personally and produced any evidence to show that he personally went there and filed the joining report being physically present in the office. The petitioner through his affidavits as well as through the annexures has shown that he personally went to the office of the corporation at Chittagong and filed his joining report on 31-3-94 and again on 2nd of April, 1994. We have gone through the repeated joining reports as annexed by the petitioner and it appears to us that in the joining report the petitioner has stated the background of the case as well as the judgment and decree passed by the courts and at the same time he expressed his sufferings in different manners in as much as he was terminated from service in 1982 and he got a favourable result from the Appellate Division in the year 1994. So, his joining report clearly shows that he wanted to join his service as Secretary of the Corporation in pursuance of the judgment of the courts including the highest court of the country, but he had not made any condition in his joining letter to the effect that unless and until his promotion and other matters are settled, he cannot join as Secretary of the corporation. So, we fine from the record that the petitioner did not put any condition in the matter of joining his service as secretary of the Corporation. The other matters which he mentioned in the repeated joining reports cannot be treated in any manner as condition to the effect that unless and until those conditions were fulfilled, he could not join his service. So, we find no substance in the submission of Mr Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed that he submitted a conditional joining report, rather it appears that he repeatedly requested the Contemner No.1 to allow him to join his service as Secretary of the Corporation but he was not allowed to join by the Contemner No. 1. 

 22. Mr Khandaker further submits thin he was not physically present in the office to submit his joining report and there is no evidence to that effect in the whole record. We may simply say, it is 'an absurd story that after winning the case through legal battle for about 12 years, the petitioner did not personally go there and submit his joining report in the office Nobody in this world will believe such a story. Even a child of yesterday cannot but feel shy to believe a story that after fighting the battle for long 12 years from 1982 to 1994 and after winning the case and having the decree in his favour in all the courts the petitioner did not go to the office of the corporation personally and submit his joining report. The petitioner has been suffering since 1982 and he got decree and favourable orders from the court of Subordinate Judge right upto the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court and it appears that he went there personally and submitted repeated joining reports to the contemner No. 1 to allow him to join as the Secretary of the corporation in view of the judgment and decree passed by the courts including the highest Court of the country, So, we find that submissions made by Mr Khandaker Mahabubuddin Ahmed have no substance. 

 23. We may look into the other materials on record. The petitioner has annexed the orders of the Ministries and he has shown that on five occasions the Government in the Ministry of Shipping sent five letters, directing the Contemner No. I to reinstate the petitioner to his service as Secretary of the Corporation in view of the judgment and decree passed by the highest Court of the country. The Contemner No. 1 being an Additional Secretary in rank had got so much audacity that even being a Government officer he ignored and dishonoured the directions of the Ministry for five times. This shows the unsusual conduct and character of the contemner No.I being Managing Director of the Corporation. It may be mentioned that whether there is enmity or not in between the Contemner No. I and the petitioner is immaterial, but we are to see from the materials on record as to whether the contemner No. I had violated and showed dishonour to the verdict of the court. 

 24. When the Rule was issued on 5-5-94 Contemner No. I was the Managing Director of the Corporation. It appears that even after issuance of the Rule and after repeated directions of the Government he willfully ignored the directions and showed dishonour to the court's judgment and after issuance of the contempt Rule he was acting in his own way showing total disrespect to the court's judgment. It appears from the record that when for the 5th time the contemner No. I disobeyed the order of the Ministry, the Ministry asked the Establishment Division for withdrawing the Contemner No. I from the post of Managing Director of the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation and with the concurrence of the Establishment Division the Ministry of Shipping had withdrawn him by letter dated 15-4-95 from the post of the Managing Director of the Shipping Corporation. It appears that in pursuance of the direction of the Ministry he had to hand over the charge to another person of the Corporation on 16-4-95. Even before handing over the charge he had not shown any respect to the court's judgment by allowing the petitioner to join his post as Secretary of the Corporation. The first joining report was submitted in the year 1989 after obtaining the decree. After obtaining the favourable order from the Appellant Division of the Supreme Court the petitioner again submitted his joining report on 31-3-94. 

 26. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering the materials on record, it appears to us that the Contemner No. 1 being a very high and responsible Officer as Additional Secretary of the Government and Managing Director of a Corporation had shown total disrespect to the Judgment and decree of the Courts including the Highest Court of the country, namely, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. It appears to us that with deliberate intention he had violated the judgment of the courts as well as the directives of the concerned Ministry for such a long time. So, we find that he is guilty of gross type of contempt of Court in view of the fact that he is not a layman, rather he is an educated person having the rank and status of Additional Secretary of the Ministry and he ought to have shown respect to the Court immediately. 

 27. In this connection, it may be mentioned that he was withdrawn from the Shipping Corporation by the Government and another gentleman named SM Shamsul Alam was appointed as Managing Director on 21st May, 1995. After joining as Managing Direcotor he by a letter dated 25-5-95 asked the petitioner to join his post as Secretary of the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation as per judgment of the Court. So, it appears that these gentlemen Mr SM Shamsul Alam who joined on 21st May 1995, within four days from his joining, asked the petitioner to join his service as Secretary of the Corporation in pursuance of the decree of the Court. This man Mr SM Shamsul Alam could obey the judgment of the Court within four days from the date of his joining as Managing Director, But, unfortunately, the Contemner No. 1 being in the rank of Additional Secretary failed to obey the judgment of the highest Court of the country within12 months and 16 days. This shows the difference between man and man and the officer and officer. 

 28. We have gone through the counter- affidavit of the Contemner No.1 wherein he has fully defended himself giving all the blams to the petitioner. He has not hesitated to say that it is not he, but the petitioner himself who has committed contempt of court by twisting the decree which he got from the courts, After issuance of the Contempt Rule or even before leaving the office on 16-4-95, if the Contemner No. 1 implemented the courts order by accepting the joining report of the petitioner, we could have taken a lenient view in the matter awarding sentence but it was not done. In the whole counter-affidavit of the contemner No. 1 we do not find a single word expressing sorrow, repentance, remorse of apology of any kind. So we find that this is a fit case where we should award exemplary punishment for greater interest of the society
